sentences.text: Khemlal @ Khemu Banjare S/o Sukalu Banjare Aged About 24 Years

R/o Village Sirri, Police Station Abhanpur, District : Raipur,
 Chhattisgarh.
----Applicant  Versus  State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer, Police Station  Abhanpur, District : Raipur, Chhattisgarh  ----Non-applicant For Applicant Shri C.R. Sahu, Advocate.

For State Shri Adil Minhaj, G.A.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput  Order on Board 19/01/2023  1.

This is the Second Bail Application filed under Section 439 of Code of  Criminal Procedure for grant of bail in connection with Crime  No.245/2022 registered at Police Station Abhanpur, District Raipur  (C.G.) for the offence under Sections 363,366, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.
2. Earlier bail application has been dismissed as withdrawn by this Court  vide order dated 10/10/2022 in MCRC No. 7248/2022 with liberty to  revive after examination of the prosecutrix.
3. Brief facts of the case is that the victim's father has lodged a report that
her daugher went outside from the house without informing to anyone.

On the basis of such complaint Police has registered the crime and  during investigation victim has recovered from the possession of the  present applicant.
 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the allegation against the  present applicant is false and fictitious, he is in jail since 30/06/2022,
 prosecutrix has not supported the case of the prosecution, charge-sheet  has been filed, hence he may be entitled for grant of bail.
 5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.

6. Prosecutrix and her father appeared through video conferencing from the concerned DLSA and Khemlal @ Khemu Banjare vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119510623/
1 made 'No Objection' with regard to grant of bail to the applicant.
7.

entities.text: Khemlal @ Khemu Banjare vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties, considering their rival submissions.

8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the nature of allegations against the present applicant, he is in jail since 30/06/2022, trial is likely to take some time for disposal,
prosecutrix has turned hostile before the Court below, without commenting anything on merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of applicant executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court, he shall be released on bail on the following conditions:-
(i) he shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade his from disclosing such fact to the Court (ii) he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial, and (iii) he shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to his by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
( iv )
he shall not involve himself in any offence of similar nature in future.
(v) he is restrained from meeting any of the prosecution witnesses till the conclusion of the trial.
9. It is made clear that these observations are only for the purposes of deciding the bail application.
The trial Court will decide the case on its own merits without being influenced by any observation made herein- above.
It is also made clear that the State is at liberty to move an application regarding cancellation of bail of the applicant in the event of applicant violates any of the conditions.

Sd/-
Sachin Singh Rajput Judge Kamde Khemlal @ Khemu Banjare vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119510623/
